`Timeout: 15s` per request, and the client wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`
for that timeout too. A caller cannot tell the client timeout from the
context's deadline, so `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts both in
the `failed` verdict.

**Catalog walk (DEVDESK-306, IS-03).** `ListCatalogContext(ctx, apiURL,
username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` returns `(names, truncated, err)`. It
asks `<apiURL>/v2/_catalog?n=<pageSize>` and follows `Link: rel="next"` for at
most `maxPages` pages (non-positive limits are an error). `truncated` is true
when names were left: the page cap was reached with a `next` link, more than
`maxPages*pageSize` names came back (the list is cut to that), or the `next`
link points to another origin. Each page body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger
page is an error, not a silent cut. A non-200 answer is a `*StatusError`.
Authentication is the tags' flow: Basic, then Bearer on a challenge, the token
kept across pages.

- **`next` is followed only to the same origin.** `sameOrigin` compares scheme
  and host strictly (`host` and `host:443` differ), so a registry cannot make
  the walk send the Basic credentials or the token elsewhere. A foreign or
  differently written `next` ends the walk as `truncated`, with no error.
- **HTTP 3xx redirects are not hardened**: they follow `registryHTTPClient`,
  as the tags do. The origin guard covers the `next` link only. A separate
  ticket is proposed.

## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)

Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:

- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
  an anonymous entry, D12).
- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
  `library/` applied once (D39).
- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
  with no request at all. Production uses
  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` and
  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
  registry. Steps, in order:
  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
     is returned as is, with no row.
  3. Guard R1 (before the filter): when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
     `partial` set, not an error.
  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
     others are dropped.
  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.

  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search: one per checked
  entry, so several entries on one host walk its catalog several times (IS-07).
  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
  match wins:
  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
     given in both cases;
  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
     token endpoint is a failure); any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is
     `failed`;
  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
     oversized body, invalid request.

  `ErrQueryTooShort` and `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` are returned by
  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).
| `kind` | `registry` or `group` |
| `parent` | slug of the owning group — carried by discovered members, not normally by config entries |
| `provider` | `generic`, `nexus`, `harbor`, `artifactory`, `gitlab`; declared, never sniffed from the URL |
| `auth_mode` | `credentials`, `anonymous`, or `inherit` for a member. Replaces `auth_enabled`, which is migrated at load and then dropped. |
| `repo_prefix` | what goes in front of the repository name. With `url` it is the entry's **address** (§3.18) |

**An entry is an address, not a URL** (§3.18, D39). The pair `(url, repo_prefix)`
is what a registry is reached by, and both directions derive from it — the browse
asks `<url>/v2/<prefix>/<repo>/tags/list` (through `oci.ListRegistryTags`, the one tag lister, which follows `Link` pagination), the pull reference is
`<url>/<prefix>/<repo>:<tag>` — so they cannot mean two different repositories.
That disagreement is exactly what D39 was: `NexusDetector` synthesised a member
as `host/repository/<name>`, which browses (200) and cannot pull (404), because
the Docker client puts `/v2/` first and the whole path after it.

Like `provider`, it is **declared, never sniffed**. Whether a repository answers
on a path prefix, a connector port or a subdomain is a setting on that repository
(`docker.httpPort`, `docker.httpsPort`, `docker.subdomain`), and the one endpoint
carrying it answers 403 to an ordinary pull account — the same endpoint that
would say what a group's members are. An instance that refuses one refuses both,
so guessing is not a fallback, it is the defect.

The same declaration drives the image search header (DEVDESK-308): a
`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry, its discovered members, and a declared
entry with `parent: <slug>` pointing at such a group are listed from cached
content only, so the browser's level 1 header shows them on a `Cached only`
line. The provider is read from the config (`config.IsNexusGroup`), never
guessed from the URL. See `network.md`, "Level 1 header summary".

The image search (`network.md`, `CatalogSearcher`, DEVDESK-306) reads the same
pair: it walks the catalog of the entry's host (`/v2/_catalog`, with the entry's
`auth_mode` through `credsFor`), keeps the names under `<repo_prefix>/` and
matches the typed text on the part after it. A catalog with no name under the
prefix is refused, not "no result". Each entry is walked on its own, so several
members of one host cost several walks.

Three things follow, each with a test:

- **The prefix is applied once**, in `submitSearch`. It is then already part of
  `MultiRegistryTag.Repo`, so `multiImageName` and `registryAPIURL` know nothing
  about it — teaching both would be two places free to drift.
- **A group may not declare one**, and `LoadContext` refuses it: a group is
  reachable only through its own connector, and the same trick applied to a group
  answers 404. `RegistryForm` therefore does not offer the field on a group.
- **A URL no longer identifies an entry.** Several entries share one host now, so
  `entryFor` resolves by entry key, `resultFilter` holds a key, every
  `MultiRegistryTag` carries one, and `memberKey` takes the prefix as a third
  Rule 130) reports `reasonNoImage`. `→` changes nothing and warns through
  `RegistryBrowserWarnMsg`: footer Warn `No image selected`. The `→ Open tags`
  shortcut is greyed.
- **Failed listing.** `handleMultiRegistryTagsLoaded`, when `tagsFromSearch` is
  set, leaves the table with its header only (Rule 139), shows `tagsLoadFailedText`
  (`Could not load tags`) as a 3 s footer Error, and logs
  `ERROR [oci_resources] registry tags on <alias>: <cause>` where the cause comes
  from `searchErrorCause`: no credentials, no URL. The full-name flow is
  unchanged and silent on screen (it logs `registry tags <repo> from <url>`).

`Timeout: 15s` per request, and the client wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`
for that timeout too. A caller cannot tell the client timeout from the
context's deadline, so `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts both in
the `failed` verdict.

**Catalog walk (DEVDESK-306, IS-03).** `ListCatalogContext(ctx, apiURL,
username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` returns `(names, truncated, err)`. It
asks `<apiURL>/v2/_catalog?n=<pageSize>` and follows `Link: rel="next"` for at
most `maxPages` pages (non-positive limits are an error). `truncated` is true
when names were left: the page cap was reached with a `next` link, more than
`maxPages*pageSize` names came back (the list is cut to that), or the `next`
link points to another origin. Each page body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger
page is an error, not a silent cut. A non-200 answer is a `*StatusError`.
Authentication is the tags' flow: Basic, then Bearer on a challenge, the token
kept across pages.

- **`next` is followed only to the same origin.** `sameOrigin` compares scheme
  and host strictly (`host` and `host:443` differ), so a registry cannot make
  the walk send the Basic credentials or the token elsewhere. A foreign or
  differently written `next` ends the walk as `truncated`, with no error.
- **HTTP 3xx redirects are not hardened**: they follow `registryHTTPClient`,
  as the tags do. The origin guard covers the `next` link only. A separate
  ticket is proposed.

## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)

Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:

- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
  an anonymous entry, D12).
- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
  `library/` applied once (D39).
- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
  with no request at all. Production uses
  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` and
  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
  registry. Steps, in order:
  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
     is returned as is, with no row.
  3. Guard R1 (before the filter): when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
     `partial` set, not an error.
  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
     others are dropped.
  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.

  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search: one per checked
  entry, so several entries on one host walk its catalog several times (IS-07).
  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
  match wins:
  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
     given in both cases;
  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
     token endpoint is a failure); any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is
     `failed`;
  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
     oversized body, invalid request.

  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).

## DEVDESK-311 (IS-07) : un seul parcours de `_catalog` par hôte et par identité, pour chaque recherche

**Questions bloquantes : aucune.** Les choix restants sont des détails, posés plus bas en hypothèses prudentes. Je n'ai rien modifié et je n'ai rien écrit sur disque.

### Constat (code de main)
- `startImageSearch` (`internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_flow.go:87`) lance un `searchImagesCmd` par entrée cochée, chacun sous `context.WithTimeout(lotCtx, 15s)`. Chaque `CatalogSearcher.Search` (`internal/imagesearch/catalog.go:45`) appelle alors `list(...)` : avec N membres sur le même hôte, on obtient N parcours identiques, puisque le parcours ne dépend que de `APIURL`, `Username`, `Password` et des constantes de pages. Le filtrage par préfixe et par texte vient après.
- Les membres d'un groupe tiennent leurs identifiants du parent (`credsFor` lit `parentURL`) et ont la même `APIURL` quand le routage passe par un chemin (`registryAPIURL(m.URL)`). Un membre exposé sur un port ou un sous-domaine a une autre `APIURL` : il ne sera jamais regroupé, et c'est voulu.

### Options
| | Principe | Pour | Contre |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Regrouper avant le lancement | La vue (ou un `MultiSearcher`) partitionne les cibles, lance un Cmd par groupe et reçoit un message à N réponses | Explicite | La vue doit savoir qui passe par le catalogue, ce qui fait fuir la logique de `ByRegistry` ou impose une assertion de type sur `b.searcher`. Il faut un nouveau message. Le compte de `pendingSearches` change (un Cmd pour N réponses). Les faux `Searcher` qui comptent un appel par registre (IS-01 c.1) cassent |
| **B. Mémo propre au lot, porté par le contexte du lot** | `imagesearch.WithSharedWalks(ctx)` attache un mémo au contexte du lot ; `CatalogSearcher` le consulte | La vue change d'une ligne. L'interface `Searcher`, les messages, `pendingSearches`, la génération, l'`Outcome` par entrée, l'en-tête et `Cached only` restent tels quels. Le mémo meurt avec le lot, donc il ne peut pas y avoir de cache entre deux recherches | Dépendance implicite par valeur de contexte (à documenter). C'est le contexte du premier appelant qui gouverne le parcours |
| C. `x/sync/singleflight` | Dédoublonnage pendant le vol | Code connu | Nouvelle dépendance. Surtout, il oublie la clé dès la fin du vol : un Cmd ordonnancé après la fin du parcours repasse au registre, et le test de l'AC1 devient instable. **Rejeté** |

**Recommandation : B.** C'est un mémo (map de `walkCall` gardée pendant tout le lot), pas un singleflight.

### Clé de regroupement (aucun secret en clair)
- `walkKey{apiURL string; identity [32]byte}`
- `apiURL` = `strings.TrimSuffix(t.APIURL, "/")`, comparée exactement. Hypothèse prudente : pas de normalisation de casse ni de port. Rater un regroupement coûte seulement un parcours de plus, alors qu'en fusionner deux à tort peut servir à une entrée un catalogue qui n'est pas le sien.
- `identity` = HMAC-SHA256 avec une clé aléatoire de 32 octets tirée par lot (`crypto/rand`), calculé sur `len(user)‖user‖len(pass)‖pass`. Ni le nom d'utilisateur ni le mot de passe ne sont stockés ou comparés en clair dans la map. La clé n'est jamais journalisée et la clé HMAC n'est pas dérivable hors du lot.
- Point de confidentialité : Harbor, Artifactory et GitLab filtrent le catalogue selon les droits du compte. On ne partage donc **jamais** un parcours entre deux identités : `anonymous` et `credentials` donnent deux clés (AC4).
- Hypothèse : la clé porte sur les identifiants **effectifs**. Une entrée en `credentials` sans secret stocké envoie exactement les mêmes requêtes qu'une entrée anonyme, et partage donc son parcours. Le test de l'AC4 utilise donc un secret stocké.

### Concurrence, annulation, état d'échec
- Meneur : le premier appel d'une clé enregistre `walkCall{done chan struct{}}` sous mutex, lance `list` **hors** mutex avec son propre ctx, puis renseigne `names`, `truncated` et `err` et fait `defer close(done)`.
- Suiveurs : `select { <-call.done | <-ctx.Done() }`.
- `names` est partagé en lecture seule. `CatalogSearcher` ne fait que le parcourir avec `range` et construit `all` à neuf ; ce sera vérifié avec `-race`.
- Annulation : rien ne change. `beginRequests` et `abandonLot` annulent le ctx parent, donc le meneur et les suiveurs s'arrêtent ; la génération écarte les réponses tardives. Le mémo est créé dans le contexte du lot, donc un nouveau lot repart toujours d'un nouveau mémo.
- Échéance : le parcours tourne sous les 15 s du meneur. Comme tous les Cmd du lot partent ensemble avec le même délai, c'est équivalent à aujourd'hui. Si le meneur tombe sur son échéance, les suiveurs reçoivent la **même** erreur.
- AC3 : chaque membre reçoit le même `err`, donc `Classify` donne le même `Outcome` (`failed`, ou `refused` sur un 401/403). Il y a toujours un `ImageSearchResultMsg` par entrée, donc l'`Outcome` par registre reste par entrée et la ligne `Failed:` de D136 liste les trois libellés.
- Verdict de DEVDESK-303 : `Classify` ne bouge pas.
- `Cached only` (DEVDESK-308) : il reste calculé par entrée (`entryCachedOnly`), aucun effet.
- `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` et `Partial` restent calculés **par membre** à partir du parcours commun : un membre peut être `refused` pendant qu'un autre est `ok`. Ce n'est pas un échec partagé.
- Journal : un échec partagé produit N lignes `ERROR` (une par membre, avec son alias), toutes sans secret (`searchErrorCause`). Hypothèse : on les garde, puisque chaque verdict est journalisé.
- Risque structurel : si un jour les échéances divergent d'une entrée à l'autre, l'échéance du meneur s'imposera aux suiveurs. À noter dans le code.

### Plan (effort S confirmé)

**Étape 1 — `internal/imagesearch` : le mémo de lot.**
Nouveau fichier `walks.go` :
```go
func WithSharedWalks(ctx context.Context) context.Context
type walkShare struct { secret [32]byte; mu sync.Mutex; calls map[walkKey]*walkCall }
type walkKey struct { apiURL string; identity [sha256.Size]byte }
type walkCall struct { done chan struct{}; names []string; truncated bool; err error }
func (s *walkShare) keyFor(t Target) walkKey
func (s *walkShare) walk(ctx context.Context, t Target, list CatalogLister) ([]string, bool, error)
func walkCatalog(ctx context.Context, t Target, list CatalogLister) ([]string, bool, error) // mémo si présent, sinon appel direct
```
Dans `catalog.go:45`, `list(...)` devient `walkCatalog(ctx, t, list)`. La vérification `ErrQueryTooShort` reste avant, sans parcours.

Tests (nouveau `walks_test.go`, avec un faux `CatalogLister` qui compte ses appels et une barrière pour forcer la concurrence) :
- 3 cibles, même API et mêmes identifiants, préfixes `a`, `b`, `c`, lancées en parallèle → 1 appel ; chaque cible ne garde que ses noms, avec sa propre `EntryKey` (AC1, AC2).
- Les mêmes appels en séquence sur un même mémo → 1 appel. C'est ce test qui distingue un mémo d'un singleflight.
- Le lister renvoie `&oci.StatusError{Code:503}` → les 3 reçoivent l'erreur et `Classify` est identique pour les 3 (AC3).
- Mêmes `APIURL`, anonyme contre user/pass → 2 appels. Même user avec deux mots de passe différents → 2 appels. Deux `APIURL` différentes → 2 appels (AC4).
- Sans `WithSharedWalks` → 3 appels (comportement inchangé). Deux mémos différents (deux lots) → 2 appels.
- Le ctx d'un suiveur est annulé pendant que le meneur est bloqué → le suiveur rend `context.Canceled` tout de suite et le meneur continue.
- Parcours tronqué partagé → `Partial` par membre, comme en D135.
- Requête d'un seul caractère avec le mémo → 0 appel.
- `fmt.Sprintf("%#v", keyFor(t))` ne contient ni le user ni le mot de passe.

Fin d'étape : `go test ./internal/imagesearch` et `mise run test-race` au vert.

**Étape 2 — câblage dans la vue et documentation (dépend de l'étape 1, rien à paralléliser).**
Dans `browser_flow.go`, `startImageSearch` : `ctx := imagesearch.WithSharedWalks(b.beginRequests())`. Le lot de tags n'est pas concerné.

Tests (nouveau `browser_catalog_share_test.go`, avec les aides existantes `catalogServer`, `wiredLikeProduction`, `runCmds`, `recvResult`, `writeDockerConfig`) :
- Groupe Nexus avec 3 membres sur l'URL d'un `httptest`, préfixes distincts → le compteur `/v2/_catalog` vaut 1. `RegistryBrowserOutcomes()` donne un verdict par `memberKey`, chaque ligne porte la clé de son membre, `Cached only` liste les 3.
- Serveur en 503 → les 3 sont `failed` et la ligne `Failed:` les liste.
- Deux registres autonomes sur la même URL, l'un `anonymous`, l'autre `credentials` avec un secret écrit par `writeDockerConfig` → 2 requêtes.
- Deux recherches successives → 2 parcours (pas de cache entre recherches).

Documentation, dans le même commit :
- `docs/architecture/network.md`, section `CatalogSearcher` : la phrase « Walks per search: one per checked entry… (IS-07) » décrit désormais le mémo de lot, la clé, la règle meneur/suiveurs et l'échec partagé.
- `docs/architecture/registries.md` : remplacer « Each entry is walked on its own, so several members of one host cost several walks ».
- Fin d'étape : `mise run check` et `mise run test-race` au vert.

### Décision à archiver
Une entrée D140 dans `docs/backlog.md` suffit ; pas d'ADR, la décision est locale et réversible. Contenu : la clé (API exacte + HMAC propre au lot), un mémo et non un singleflight (avec la raison), l'échec partagé suivi d'un verdict identique par entrée, aucun cache entre recherches, le risque sur l'échéance du meneur, et l'hypothèse Nexus.

### Hypothèse Nexus non vérifiée (IS-16)
IS-07 n'aggrave rien. Un membre exposé sur un port ou un sous-domaine a une autre `APIURL` et n'est pas regroupé. Si les membres d'un même hôte ne listent pas leurs dépôts sous leur `repo_prefix` dans `/v2/_catalog`, c'est le garde-fou R1 d'IS-03 qui le dit (`refused`), par membre, avec ou sans partage.

### Revue de sécurité
**Oui, une revue ciblée et courte est justifiée.** Elle porte sur trois points :
1. La dérivation de la clé : HMAC, clé propre au lot, aucun secret en clair.
2. L'absence de tout partage d'un catalogue filtré par compte entre deux identités.
3. Aucun secret dans les logs, ni dans un `%v` de la clé ou des erreurs propagées aux suiveurs.

### Fichiers
- À créer : `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/imagesearch/walks.go`, `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/imagesearch/walks_test.go`, `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_catalog_share_test.go`
- À modifier : `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/imagesearch/catalog.go`, `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_flow.go`, `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/docs/architecture/network.md`, `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/docs/architecture/registries.md`, `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/docs/backlog.md`
